title: The Nernst potential for potassium
caption: With 140 mM K⁺ inside, the membrane potential at which K⁺ stops flowing is E = (26.7 mV) ln(c_out/140) at 310 K. At the usual 5 mM outside it is -89 mV, close to a neuron's resting potential; raising outside K⁺ depolarises the cell.
alt: Nernst potential in millivolts against outside potassium concentration, a logarithmic curve rising from about minus 130 at 1 millimolar through minus 89 at 5 to zero at 140.
description: E_K = (RT/F) ln(c_out / c_in), RT/F = 26.7 mV at 310 K, c_in = 140 mM.
